title: Pre-trade devil's advocate: adversarial challenge before high-conviction buys
description: The BUY pipeline has no adversarial check. Review Agent recommends → Manager Agent approves → trade executes. The IRM reviews decisions post-hoc but can't stop a trade in-flight. Proposal: for any BUY with conviction ≥4★, spawn a 'BearCaseAgent' that reads the same thesis and produces a structured counter-argument: what would have to be true for this trade to fail? What's the base rate of success for this sector/pattern? Does the canary context invalidate the thesis? Manager Agent sees both the bull and bear case before deciding. This won't block good trades — it will surface hidden risks on marginal ones.
auto_fix_hint: Add BearCaseAgent class to manager_agent.py. Instantiate it inline when conviction >= 4 before placing the order. It reads the pick's sector, RSI, recent news context (from canary/geopolitical data), and writes a structured counter-case to `data/bear_cases.json`. Manager Agent's final decision logs both cases for IRM post-trade review.

title: Replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 188/30)
description: The firm is on day 188/30 of a fixed trading window. Fixed-window evaluation creates end-of-horizon distortions: agents and managers behave differently when the 'clock is running out'. More importantly, when day 30 ends, institutional memory resets. Proposal: remove the 30-day limit. Run perpetually. Generate a quarterly benchmark report (vs. SPY, QQQ, sector ETFs) every 63 trading days. Evaluate the firm on rolling 30/63/252-day Sharpe ratio, not a single fixed window. This is how real hedge funds measure themselves.
auto_fix_hint: In state.json, replace `paper_day` counter with `trading_day_total` (never resets). Add `quarterly_benchmark_day` that triggers a benchmark report every 63 days. In main.py, remove the day-30 termination condition. Report generator shows trailing 30/63-day Sharpe vs. benchmark instead of 'Day X/30'.

title: Build a targeted short book for CRITICAL/HIGH risk regimes
description: In CRITICAL risk regimes (current: HIGH), the firm deploys SH as a broad inverse hedge. SH tracks the S&P 500 inverse — it captures index-level moves but misses the outsized drawdowns in weakest names. Proposal: when CRO declares CRITICAL, the R&D leader runs a 'short scan' pass alongside the normal long scan, looking for names with: deteriorating fundamentals, failed support levels, high short interest already, and negative sector momentum. These enter a separate 'short book' with its own position limits and stop-loss rules (inverted: stop-gain not stop-loss).
auto_fix_hint: Add `short_book_enabled` flag to config.py, gated on CRO level. R&D leader gets a `--scan-shorts` mode that inverts scoring criteria. Manager Agent executes short sells via Alpaca (supported in paper mode). Separate MAX_SHORT_POSITION_PCT (suggest 3%) and SHORT_STOP_GAIN_PCT (15%).

title: Replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 189/30)
description: The firm is on day 189/30 of a fixed trading window. Fixed-window evaluation creates end-of-horizon distortions: agents and managers behave differently when the 'clock is running out'. Generate a quarterly benchmark report (vs. SPY, QQQ, sector ETFs) every 63 trading days. Evaluate the firm on rolling 30/63/252-day Sharpe ratio, not a single fixed window. This is how real hedge funds measure themselves.
